Exercise 15.7.31 — Six Iterated Integrals over a Parabolic Solid

Problem. Express the integral ∭Ef(x,y,z) dV \iiint_E f(x,y,z)\, dV ∭E​f(x,y,z)dV as an iterated integral in six different ways, where EEE is the solid bounded by the surfaces y=x2,z=0,y+2z=4. y = x^2, \qquad z = 0, \qquad y + 2z = 4. y=x2,z=0,y+2z=4.

Part 1 — The six orders of integration

Step 1.1: Describe the solid.

The plane y+2z=4y + 2z = 4y+2z=4 meets the plane z=0z = 0z=0 in the line y=4y = 4y=4, and it meets the parabolic cylinder y=x2y = x^2y=x2 along the space curve (x, x2, (4−x2)/2)(x,\, x^2,\, (4-x^2)/2)(x,x2,(4−x2)/2). In the zzz-direction the solid lies between the plane z=0z = 0z=0 and the plane y+2z=4y + 2z = 4y+2z=4; in the yyy-direction it lies between the parabolic cylinder y=x2y = x^2y=x2 and the line y=4y = 4y=4. Hence the solid is

E={(x,y,z):x2≤y≤4,  0≤z≤(4−y)/2}. E = \{(x,y,z): x^2 \le y \le 4,\; 0 \le z \le (4-y)/2\}. E={(x,y,z):x2≤y≤4,0≤z≤(4−y)/2}.

The condition z≥0z \ge 0z≥0 in the solid is equivalent to y≤4y \le 4y≤4, and the condition y≥x2y \ge x^2y≥x2 bounds xxx by ∣x∣≤2|x| \le 2∣x∣≤2. Above each point (x0,y0)(x_0, y_0)(x0​,y0​) of the parabolic region Dxy={x2≤y≤4}D_{xy} = \{x^2 \le y \le 4\}Dxy​={x2≤y≤4} the solid rises from z=0z = 0z=0 to z=(4−y0)/2z = (4 - y_0)/2z=(4−y0​)/2, and the height is largest, equal to 222, along the parabola y=x2y = x^2y=x2 itself. The notable points of the solid are (0,0,0)(0,0,0)(0,0,0), the lowest point of the parabolic edge (x,x2,0)(x, x^2, 0)(x,x2,0); (0,0,2)(0,0,2)(0,0,2), the highest point of the solid, on the curved edge (x,x2,(4−x2)/2)(x, x^2, (4-x^2)/2)(x,x2,(4−x2)/2); and (±2,4,0)(\pm 2, 4, 0)(±2,4,0), where the parabola y=x2y = x^2y=x2 meets the line y=4y = 4y=4.

Step 1.2: The six iterated integrals.

Solving x2≤y≤4x^2 \le y \le 4x2≤y≤4 for xxx gives ∣x∣≤y|x| \le \sqrt{y}∣x∣≤y​ with 0≤y≤40 \le y \le 40≤y≤4; solving it together with z≥0z \ge 0z≥0 gives 0≤z≤(4−x2)/20 \le z \le (4-x^2)/20≤z≤(4−x2)/2 with x2≤yx^2 \le yx2≤y, i.e. −4−2z≤x≤4−2z-\sqrt{4-2z} \le x \le \sqrt{4-2z}−4−2z​≤x≤4−2z​ for 0≤z≤20 \le z \le 20≤z≤2. Derivation of the limits. The solid is cut by z=0z = 0z=0, the plane z=(4−y)/2z = (4-y)/2z=(4−y)/2, and the parabola y=x2y = x^2y=x2. The xxx-limits come from two sources: when yyy (or zzz) is fixed first, ∣x∣≤y|x| \le \sqrt{y}∣x∣≤y​ (or ∣x∣≤4−2z|x| \le \sqrt{4-2z}∣x∣≤4−2z​); when xxx is fixed first, xxx itself runs over [−2,2][-2,2][−2,2] because x2≤4x^2 \le 4x2≤4. The yyy-limits come from x2≤y≤4x^2 \le y \le 4x2≤y≤4 when xxx is fixed, or from 0≤y≤40 \le y \le 40≤y≤4 when xxx is the variable solved for (with the corresponding zzz-bound). Each order above follows by choosing which variable is fixed outermost and solving the three inequalities for the two variables that remain.

Step 1.3: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates all six orders with the constant integrand f=1f = 1f=1 using SymPy. Every order returns the exact volume 128/15≈8.5333128/15 \approx 8.5333128/15≈8.5333, confirming that the six sets of limits all describe the same solid. The figure scripts part1_figure1.py and part1_figure2.py produce the two figures embedded above.
